docs.title: My Learning Wiki: Zero to Mastery book
docs.text:
Welcome to my hands-on wiki. Every chapter is plain Markdown, and the whole site rebuilds automatically when you push a change.

  • Code first

    Short explanations, lots of runnable examples.

  • Experiment

    If in doubt, run the code and see what happens.

  • Visualize

    Numbers on a page get confusing, so draw them.

  • Ask questions

    Stuck? Open a discussion on the repository.

docs.title: Who is this for?
docs.text: Beginners who want to learn by doing.

docs.title: What are the prerequisites?
docs.text:
1. A few months of experience with the basics.
  2. A browser and a willingness to learn (the most important one).

docs.title: How do I approach this?
docs.text:
1. Code along. Type the examples yourself.
  2. Explore and experiment. Change things and see what breaks.
  3. Do the exercises. You will get stuck, and that's normal.
  4. Share your work. Teaching others is the best way to learn.

docs.title: Do I need to take things in order?
docs.text:
The chapters build on each other, but feel free to jump around.

Happy learning!

docs.title: Exercises
docs.text:
1. Change the message and run the example again.
  2. Print your own name.

docs.title: Extra-curriculum
docs.text: • Read the official documentation for the tool you're learning.

docs.title: The steps
docs.text:
1. Get the data ready.
  2. Build or pick a model.
  3. Fit the model to the data.
  4. Evaluate the results.
  5. Improve through experimentation.
  6. Save and reload your work.

docs.title: Exercises
docs.text:
1. Write the six steps in your own words.
  2. Pick a small problem and walk it through the workflow.
